name: Ecdysterone
lead: Ecdysterone, or 20-hydroxyecdysone, is the main molting hormone of insects and crustaceans and is also found in plants such as spinach and Cyanotis. It is sold as a supplement and is being developed as an investigational drug for some muscle conditions.

A widely cited study in young men reported greater muscle gains with high-dose ecdysterone alongside training, but replication is lacking and other findings are mixed, so the evidence remains preliminary.

paras: In rodents ecdysterone stimulates muscle protein synthesis without androgen receptor activity, with evidence pointing to estrogen receptor beta and downstream Akt signalling. Human mechanism data are thin.
Acute toxicity appears low. It is sold as a supplement but the World Anti-Doping Agency has monitored it, and product purity is variable. Long-term human safety is not established.
